entradas.text: "Most of the political criminals from the Soll era are old communists and Bludish nationalists."
"The amnesty will surely be controversial. But it should also reflect good with the Bludish and the left."
"The Fair Trade Commission will be essential in dealing with the monopolies."
"It was time we established a body that regulates economic competition."
"Privatization of the prison system is going to be very controversial."
"But the increased number of detainees has been pushing state prisons to their limits. This will surely lift a burden from the government."
"But this will surely lift a burden from the government."
"De-Sollinization, huh?"
"You've got some balls, Anton. Putting Soll on trial and removing his cult of personality..."
"I never thought this day would come."
"You've got some balls, Anton. I knew you wouldn't stop at taking one of his portraits down."
"You've got some balls, Anton. I never thought this would be possible."
"Looks like Mrs. Walda or the First Lady had a huge influence on your decision."

"Addressing the inequality of genders in our education will show them that our administration cares. Some of the changes might be disruptive, yes, but it was time we pursued equal rights. The women marches were starting to get annoying too."
"This will, however, anger a lot of conservatives. Let us not forget the fact that our biggest bulk of voters aren't socially liberal. This is a risky move right before the elections."

"Sir, this may create a lot of frustration and anger among the conservatives. Let us not forget the fact that we are openly attacking the founder of our party. A very risky move right before the elections."

"Yes, but it will anger a lot of the nationalists and Sollists. If we cannot make the socialists or the Bludish vote for us instead of their primary parties of choice, this amnesty might be damaging for us."
"Half of the country is women, Lucian."
"Yes, but how many of them are actively involved with these demands for change? It is a mistake to make generalisations because of a vocal minority. But let's move on."
"Rural Education Institutes, huh? The last person I've heard mention that was Artor Wisci. This is a controversial topic."
"Sollists always protested the idea of educating villagers and farmers like the urban workers. They claim it will lead Malenyevist ideas to surge in the rural."
"They're not entirely wrong. It is difficult to determine how it will affect our votes though. The rural voters are a very important base for us, and maybe this will help us win them over."
"Honestly, I couldn't care less, but banning all religious symbols from public life feels a little extreme. While religion is not the major force it used to be..."
"...I doubt the conservatives would like this. Even Tarquin Soll didn't go that far."

"This sort of laicist action will definitely spark a reaction from the faithful. It's true that Soll was a secularist, but he knew not to anger devout Nurists too much. We'll need to be careful not to let this get out of hand."
"Legalizing firearms... I'm not entirely on board with this."
"Our term started with an assassination, for God's sake, Anton! Do you really think handing out guns will solve Sordland's problems?"
"I'm afraid it has the potential to add more fuel to the fire, yes... But let's not question the President, Mr. Vectern."
"I see. We are bringing back capital punishment... Not a bad idea where some crimes are concerned."
"Soll must have executed thousands before he removed it, but he's still remembered as a hero for getting rid of it. Bringing it back will likely result in a huge outcry."
"The NFP has been advocating for this for far too long. It might make the nationalists happy, but it could also bring back dark memories for leftists and minorities."
"Of course, it depends on who ends up on the wrong side of the firing squad."
"Not everything is about votes, Lucian."
entradas.menu: "Not everything is about votes, Lucian."

entradas.text: "It is the 20th century and we still don't guarantee some basic rights for our women. This is unacceptable."
entradas.menu: "It is the 20th century and we still don't guarantee some basic rights for our women. This is unacceptable."

entradas.text: "I understand your concerns but this is my decision."
entradas.menu: "I understand your concerns but this is my decision."

entradas.text: "This is big, Anton."
"Purging the General Staff... I hope it works. We can finally curb the power of the military over Sordish politics."
"The Generals will not like this, but there is nothing they can do about it. As long as we are swift, they won't have the time to organize and plan something... *treacherous*."
Following a brief discussion, I took notes about my decisions.
"Sending experienced teachers and doctors where they're most needed is a great plan to bring our rural areas forward. This might prove to be very useful in the long term."
"A true patriot shouldn't have a problem serving in our underdeveloped regions, but, they will likely protest for being forced to relocate either way."
"Even if the state covers all their relocation expenses, this may result in quite the opposition."
"The Central Bank gained its independence during Alphonso's term. Backtracking from that decision so quickly might be damaging."
"But it will help us control the economy better. The State should have significant control over its own money to be able to plan ahead."
"Edith will be pissed."
"Yes. We will likely lose international trust. It can scare off foreign investors in a time of need."
He laughed.
"But anyway..."
"It's great that we'll be giving out free medicine. Our poorer regions definitely suffered from the lack of it."
"However, this will put a huge burden on our government budget. It will also be very difficult to build the infrastructure around it. It must be provided equally and efficiently."
"Thankfully, this can become a very popular policy. I believe it will reflect very well on the vote, especially with the rural and the poor, if it's executed correctly."
"I see. We are only decreasing retirement age. Well, this was a very popular demand. It's a good choice."
"But it will be a huge burden for our government to provide for so many people."
"Yes. It will have serious complications in the future. However, it is also true that this will reflect very positively in the upcoming elections. It's what the public asked for."
"It's great that we're expanding government's influence on the new media. Such an institution like the Supreme Council of Sordish Radio and Television will give us more control over it."
"I want them to be independent, and only regulate the content according to some standards."

entradas.text: "Yeah..."
"I very much support your decision to form a regulatory body for radio and television. Television is the future. It's great that we all understand this."
"Interested to see how the Oligarchs would react."
"Of course, sir."
"Well, we both respect your decisions, Anton."
"So... You decided not to sign anything."
"I don't think it's the right time."
entradas.menu: "I don't think it's the right time."

entradas.text: "I won't force laws like Soll did. It's the Assembly's job to make laws."

entradas.text: "N-Nothing."
"It's funny you think that way. Using your powers for good could have helped with the next elections."
Lucian raised an eyebrow.
"Not in Sordland. But I respect your ideals, sir."
"Let's not question the President, Petr."
"But now that everything's settled, I should get to work. We'll catch up soon."
Lucian looked at his watch.
"We actually have six more minutes."
"But very well. Let's call it here."
"Thank you both."

entradas.text: "There is one more thing."
He placed a stack of paper in front of me.
"Ms. Graf has sent you the plans for the abolishment of the Special Zone."
"We can still try running it through the Assembly, if you decide to sign it."
"Ms. Morgna has sent you the plans for the Semi-Autonomous Zone of Bergia."
"We can still try running it through the Assembly, if you decide to sign it."
"It's too late now. You can take it back."
I signed the documents.

entradas.text: "If you say so."
"All right. It's the Assembly's decision now."
"Approving the new Semi-Autonomous Zone could be the most major decision you've made today."
"Nobody but you could have done something like this, Anton."
"Sir, this will alienate all of your supporters who harbor even slightly nationalist sentiments."
"Bergia gets to choose its own governor now. Let's hope whoever they elect doesn't steer them too far away from the central government."
"They will have to respect the new structure."
"You disapprove?"
"I was aware of that when I made my decision, Lucian."
Petr took a close look at the papers I signed.
"Not at all, sir."
"Of course, sir."
"Approving the abolishment of the Special Zone could be the most major decision you've made today."
"No more governor of Bergia, just cities with mayors like everywhere else. Let's hope that makes the locals feel more like they're part of this country."
"Nobody but you could have done something like this, Anton."
"While the moderates of the Bludish movement and regular citizens will likely be supportive of this..."
"The Bludish nationalists and the mainstream democratic freedom movement will be furious."
"The Assembly will not pass it anyway. I'd rather not take a popularity hit at this stage. I won't sign it."
"Enacting a new value added tax will increase our generated tax revenues but we have to understand the public reaction to a new tax levy."
"A loss in public opinion is guaranteed as the consumers and the economy adjusts to this change."
"There is a high chance this might influence the average citizen more negatively."
"We better put the newly generated money to good use."
